answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may vote on payouts. The protocol limits each account’s influence, while randomly sampled peers check claims against signed task receipts; proven duplicate identities or fabricated work lose their stake. An attacker can still create many accounts, but cannot cheaply multiply influence: each must tie up capital, and detected fraud destroys it. An island of honest agents can therefore reject a dune of bogus claims, while an opal-sized stake buys only modest influence.
